item1.justification: The trace applies element-by-element anticipation, expressly addresses the Graham factors and motivation to combine for §103, and compares claim language with specification support under §112, despite some questionable treatment of functional limitations.

item2.justification: The conclusions repeatedly identify specific limitations—such as “randomly selecting,” virtual time/location, profile similarity, and route-based location—and link them to US-2012317198-A1 or asserted specification deficiencies.

item3.justification: The final decision newly rejects claims 16 and 18 under §112 even though the office action identified them as allowable subject matter and asserted no §112 rejection against either claim.

item4.justification: The examiner’s 0.889 strictness is reflected in broad prior-art readings, resolution of functional-language ambiguity toward rejection, and refusal to allow claims having perceived disclosure deficiencies.

item5.justification: Although rejection of most claims follows the earlier analyses, the final rejection of claims 16 and 18 rests on newly introduced §112 theories that were not part of the office action or accumulated stage findings.
